subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value: TWO findings about local-placement levers, both measured on game/g3d/auxanim.c::DoTexModSeqSub at -O4 with the demo cflags, and both correcting a habit rather than adding a mechanism. (1) DECLARATION ORDER AND STATEMENT ORDER ARE INDEPENDENT LEVERS AND THE ANSWER IS OFTEN THE DECOUPLED COMBINATION. Lanes reorder declarations and their initialising statements together, because the plausible source keeps them parallel. Measured, the two are separately priced and the winning state has them DISAGREEING. From real 62 with declarations `f32 d1; f32 fr; f32 d2;` and statements `d1 = ...; fr = ...; d2 = ...;`: swapping the DECLARATIONS to `d1; d2; fr;` gave real 58; then swapping the STATEMENTS to `d1 = ...; d2 = ...; fr = ...;` gave real 42; then returning the DECLARATIONS to the original `d1; fr; d2;` while holding the new statement order gave real 30 and fuzzy 97.5373% - the best of the four combinations, and the one no lane reaches by moving a declaration together with its assignment. Enumerate the cross product, not the diagonal. (2) THE BLOCK-VERSUS-FUNCTION SCOPE CLASS BOUNDARY IS ALIGNMENT-SENSITIVE, so a NEUTRAL-IDENTICAL between the two scopes is not permanent. attempt.GC_dotexmodseqsub-needs-a-second-out-buffer-and-its-whole-map-is-the-targets-shifted-eight-bytes.20260904.v1 measured block scope and function scope returning the SAME object for this function's output buffers and recorded it as 'a proved class boundary: for this function block scope and function scope are the same allocator decision, and no further re-spelling of the scope will move it'. That was true at ITS alignment and false at the next one. With the arms' six staging floats hoisted OUT of the case blocks to function scope, re-running the same block-versus-function A/B on the buffers was decisive: block scope took real 118 -> 110 and closed the slot map to IDENTICAL. The two scope populations compete for one region, so a scope A/B measures the PAIR, and its verdict expires when the other member moves. A NEUTRAL-IDENTICAL verdict is categorical for the FORM at the alignment it was taken (probe.py's own wording is right about that) but not for the CLASS across alignments, and AGENTS.md's alignment-sensitivity rule - re-A/B recorded probes after nearby fixes rather than trusting the old sign - applies to it exactly as to a regression.
